OUR STORY

The taste we remember.

Most of us stopped saying the sambar tastes different here. We just started adding more tamarind.

When you move to Canada, the grocery aisle changes. What you cook on a Tuesday often stays the same. The dal goes on the stove, the filter coffee drips, and you reach for the chilli powder you know by the spoonful.

Happy Monk began with a question from that kitchen. What would it take to make the food we grew up with taste familiar here?

KITCHEN-TESTED

Start with the dish

For chilli powder, start with Avakaya. Raw mango, mustard and oil leave plenty of room for the chilli to show itself. For ghee, start with Mysorepak, where the aroma comes up from the pan while you stir.

There’s comfort in making something the way you remember it. Then you sit down, take a bite, and there it is.
